summary: Corporate proxy injects 'Expect: 100-continue' into CONNECT tunnel; artifact downloads stall and gRPC streaming hangs in private deploy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that in their private VPC deployment, model artifact downloads (S3 presigned flows proxied via HTTP CONNECT through their corporate web proxy) intermittently stall. The proxy is observed to inject an 'Expect: 100-continue' header into the CONNECT request path.

Impact:
- Artifact fetches for large model shards hang during initial request and time out after backend retry window.
- Long-lived gRPC streaming (model generation over redirected tunnels) hangs or resets mid-stream.
- Customer experiencing increased cold-start times for served models and failing canary rollouts.

Environment:
- Private deployment behind customer-managed egress proxy (enterprise NG-Proxy v3.8).
- Control plane connectivity fine; only artifacts and streaming flows using HTTP CONNECT to corp proxy are impacted.
- Region: us-east-1; nodes running serving-runtime 1.9.2, agent 0.17.3.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Provision private deploy nodes that route egress through corporate proxy via HTTP CONNECT.
2) Trigger model pull for gpt-open-13b (large artifact > 2GB).
3) Observe the initial TLS tunnel establishment succeeds, then the first HTTP request after CONNECT includes an injected 'Expect: 100-continue' header from the proxy.
4) Artifact fetch stalls; client waits for 100-continue reflex which never arrives; connection eventually times out.

Observed behavior:
- Stalled artifact HTTP POST/GET after CONNECT; no immediate 100 response from origin.
- Serving agent shows socket in SYN/ESTABLISHED with no progress; bytes_sent remains zero.
- gRPC sessions tunneled over the same proxy drop after client-side idle timer.

Expected behavior:
- CONNECT should be a transparent tunnel; proxy must not mutate or inject headers into the inner tunneled HTTP payload. Artifact fetches should proceed without Expect semantics applied.

Logs / captures attached:
- Packet capture excerpt (pcap) shows proxy inserts 'Expect: 100-continue' immediately after CONNECT (slices 1-40).
- Agent logs (serving-agent.log) with repeated 'artifact fetch retry' entries and 'read timeout' stack traces.
- Proxy vendor support ticket (case #CN-24211) where vendor confirms an aggressive request-normalization feature.

Notes from customer: they rolled back to an older proxy firmware and observed reduced but still present stalls; they can reproduce by toggling the 'normalize-http-headers' feature on the proxy.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: corporate proxy is performing deep-inspection / request-normalization and erroneously applying Expect semantics inside the tunneled payload. This breaks the normal CONNECT semantics where the TCP stream should be opaque.

What we tried so far:
- Replayed pcap against a lab proxy and reproduced injection of Expect header.
- Confirmed that when the tunnel is replaced with a direct NAT egress (bypassing the proxy), artifacts download successfully.
- Instrumented agent to log first 512 bytes post-CONNECT; confirmed mutated headers.
- Validated that origin (S3 presigned endpoint) never responded with 100 Continue prior to payload; server expects client to send body immediately for ranged GET/POST.

Hypothesis refinement:
- Some corporate proxies implement a feature to 'normalize' inbound HTTP semantics even inside CONNECT tunnels (buggy implementation). The injected Expect header causes origin servers or intermediate caches to stall waiting for a 100 response that will never be synthesized.

Recommended mitigations to customer:
- Disable 'normalize-http-headers' or any 'http-inspection/req-modify' feature on proxy for outbound CONNECT/443 flows.
- If proxy cannot be reconfigured, add an egress rule to bypass proxy for known artifact hostnames/prefixes (bucket endpoints) as a short-term workaround.
- Enable agent-level short-circuit: serving-agent can add 'X-Redwood-Bypass-Proxy: artifact' header on CONTROL channel to signal ops; not a full fix but helps routing decisions.

Further tests planned:
- Test forcing client to send body immediately (strip Expect from client) to see whether proxy still injects header; lab tests show proxy still injects, confirming server-side injection.
- Coordinate with proxy vendor for firmware patch.

Related artifacts and traces: pcap link: /artifacts/SUP-583412/pcap1.pcap, agent logs: /artifacts/SUP-583412/serving-agent.log

2026-03-13 11:01 Liam O'Connor (SRE): Confirmed reproduction in lab using customer's proxy config. Proxy injects Expect header inside CONNECT tunnel. Marking as Sev1 due to production model pulls failing.

2026-03-13 14:24 Elena M. (Customer): We disabled header normalization on a test proxy and model pulls succeeded. Production proxy change requires change control window next week; need a workaround until then.

2026-03-14 08:32 Vendor Support (NG-Proxy): Vendor acknowledges a bug in 3.8.x families where CONNECT stream is subject to header normalization when 'http-normalize' is enabled. Patch scheduled for 3.8.5.
2026-03-14 10:05 Priya Shah (Support): Updated customer with vendor confirmation and provided step-by-step bypass guide. Customer scheduled production window for 2026-03-20 to disable normalization.

resolution: Workaround implemented: customer will whitelist artifact hostnames to bypass the corporate proxy for CONNECT flows until vendor patch arrives. Vendor to release patch 3.8.5 to stop header normalization inside CONNECT tunnels. Follow-ups: verify post-patch artifact fetch stability and add an optional agent-side guard to detect mutated headers and fail early with clearer error message. Ticket will be closed after successful validation in production post-2026-03-20 window.
